key_insight: Patients most vulnerable to membership inference largely remained the same across tested training configurations, enabling early privacy-risk screening with four small models.
clinical_relevance: Screening before production-model training could help clinical AI teams identify patient records at risk of training-set membership disclosure.
method: Measured patient-level vulnerability to membership inference attacks.
Compared risk across training recipes, architectures and initializations.
Developed a four-model screening tool and assessed protection without removing flagged records.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 7,789 models across six clinical datasets and four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models; stronger weight decay reduced the exposed cohort by up to threefold.
watch_item: The abstract does not report screening accuracy or establish whether protection strategies reliably safeguard flagged patients.
paper_title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
